formal.statement: theorem Nat.descFactorial_zero : ((x0 : AxNat) -> Eq.{1} AxNat (AxNat.descFactorial x0 AxNat.zero) (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero))

notes:
formal.statement is `Kernel::render_lean` of the admitted type, taken verbatim from `nat_theorem_inventory`, not transcribed by hand. `AxNat` is the kernel's CONSTRUCTED inductive `Nat` (the `Ax` is *axeyum*, not *axiomatized*) -- the `nat` prelude's trusted surface measures zero.

`Nat.descFactorial` did not exist before this lane; it was one of three definitions (`Nat.ascFactorial`, `Nat.descFactorial`, `Nat.multichoose`) named as blocking five open `F:ml430-nat-*` facts. This fact does NOT flip any `F:ml430-nat-descfactorial-*` mirror fact by hand -- this kernel's `Nat.descFactorial` is our own construction (structural recursion via `define_binary`, mirroring Mathlib's own equations exactly, but proved independently), not an import of Mathlib's proof, so claiming their statements verbatim would be the checker-that-cannot-fail defect this repository explicitly guards against. Those mirror facts (`F:ml430-nat-descfactorial-le-2b8cc09a`, `-of-lt-fbcf5d26`, `-one-d4856d4a`, `-self-899fc0e0`, `-zero-966b01df`, `F:ml430-nat-factorial-dvd-descfactorial-bbf6124f`) remain untouched by this lane; `F:ml430-nat-descfactorial-one-d4856d4a` happens to already be `proved` through a wholly separate producer (the Lean/Mathlib import route, evidence id `autogenesis-operation-13843f88b89e9a23`), unrelated to this kernel construction.

The existence of the DEFINITION `Nat.descFactorial` is entailed by this row rather than separately checked: the statement mentions `AxNat.descFactorial`, and `Kernel::add_declaration` cannot admit a type naming a constant the environment does not contain.
